## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

178	def anchors():
179	    out, status = {}, {}
180	    for ln in (ROOT / "governance/functional-taxonomy.md").read_text().splitlines():
181	        m = re.match(r"\|\s*`(AX-[A-Z-]+)`\s*\|[^|]*\|([^|]*)\|([^|]*)\|\s*([A-Z]+)\s*\|", ln)
182	        if m:
183	            out[m.group(1)] = set(re.findall(r"\b[bde]\d{3,4}\b", m.group(2)))
184	            status[m.group(1)] = m.group(4)
185	    return out, status

188	def main():
189	    c = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{ROOT}/data/guidebook.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
190	    c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
191	    ax, axstat = anchors()
192	    idn = {r["identity_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_taxonomy_identity where status='active'")}
193	    need = {r["need_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from access_needs")}
194	    icf = {r["icf_code"]: r for r in c.execute("select * from base_icf")}
195	    imap, nmap = {}, {}
196	    for r in c.execute("select * from identity_icf_map where retired_at is null order by link_id"):
197	        imap.setdefault((r["identity_code"], r["icf_code"]), []).append(r)
198	    for r in c.execute("select * from access_need_icf"):
199	        nmap[(r["need_code"], r["icf_code"])] = r
200	    nneeds = c.execute("select count(*) from access_needs").fetchone()[0]
201	    held = {}
202	    for (n, code) in nmap: held.setdefault(code, set()).add(n)
203	    common = {code for code, ns in held.items() if len(ns) * 2 > nneeds}
204	    errors, triples, withheld, dropped, seen = [], [], [], [], set()
205	    for p in PAIRS:
206	        I, N = p["i"], p["n"]
207	        if I not in idn: errors.append(f"{I}: not an active identity"); continue
208	        if N not in need: errors.append(f"{N}: not a need"); continue
209	        ntext = " | ".join(filter(None, [need[N]["absorbs"], need[N]["design_obligation"], need[N]["notes"]] +
210	                                  [r["notes"] for (nn, _), r in nmap.items() if nn == N]))
211	        itext = " | ".join(filter(None, [idn[I]["display_name"], idn[I]["description"]] +
212	                                  [r["mechanism"] for (ii, _), rs in imap.items() if ii == I for r in rs]))
213	        if p["qn"] not in ntext: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: need quote not found in the need's records: {p['qn']!r}")
214	        if p["qi"] not in itext: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: identity quote not found in the identity's records: {p['qi']!r}")
215	        for path, sub in p.get("rec", []):
216	            if sub not in (ROOT / path).read_text(): errors.append(f"{I}x{N}: record {path} lacks {sub!r}")
217	        for code, axis, tie in p["codes"]:
218	            if code not in icf: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: code not in base_icf"); continue
219	            if (I, N, code) in seen: errors.append(f"{I}x{N}x{code}: listed twice"); continue
220	            seen.add((I, N, code))
221	            in_i, in_n = (I, code) in imap, (N, code) in nmap

## Findings, worst first

### F1. BLOCKER. The E3 warrants say "no project record states" the link; two project records do
- **Rows:** BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330, d350, e125, e340 (4).
- **Claim:** "that aphasia follows stroke is general medical knowledge that no project record states".
- **Evidence against:**
  - `references/website/data/populations.json` (tracked), Neurological and Acquired Brain Injury profile: "ABI; stroke sequelae (unilateral neglect, navigation impairment, aphasia, hemiplegia)".
  - `governance/functional-taxonomy.md` section 4, NEU row ("FDA term `ABI` resolves here"): maps to "COG-O, AMB, ARO, COM-E". The d330/d350 anchors come from AX-COM-E.
- **Record cutting the other way, not mentioned:** the same file, line 314, lists "aphasia/dysarthria (COM-E)" as a deferred candidate profile of its own. Filing aphasia under BRAIN is a disposition the taxonomy has not made.
- **Command:** `grep -rIl -i aphasia --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=transcripts .`
- **False if:** both passages are absent or not about stroke/ABI.

### F2. BLOCKER. The COM|A-TIME warrant attributes a quote to the wrong cell and rests on an inference the batch applies inconsistently
- **Row:** COM|A-TIME|b164.

A-TIME's `absorbs` is "slow processing, motor delay, AAC use, screen-reader navigation, translation, distraction". The phrase is in `access_need_icf.notes` for (A-TIME, b164). The script searches absorbs, obligation, notes and map notes, then labels every hit "absorbs". This is the only one of 34 pairs where the hit is outside `absorbs`.
- **Second false-leaning claim:** "that the identity … carries brain fog is not stated in a project record". Taxonomy section 4 maps `LCOV` to "STA (PEM), THR, COG-O". "Brain fog" is not there verbatim, but a cognitive-demand mapping for long COVID is a record.
- **Inconsistency:** A-LOWLOAD's `absorbs` names "brain fog" outright. The same inference would support COM|A-LOWLOAD, which the batch lacks.
- **Coverage:** this row is the only row for need A-TIME. None of the need's six absorbed terms produced a pair.
- **False if:** `select absorbs from access_needs where need_code='A-TIME'` contains "brain fog".

### F3. BLOCKER. 20 warrants append a WHO title from memory to a sentence that begins "governance/functional-taxonomy.md 2.1 lists …"
- **Shape:** "… lists b210 among the ICF anchors of AX-VIS-N, the seeing-function anchor …". The listing is derived; the gloss is the session's recall, joined by a comma. `base_icf.title` is NULL for each of these codes, and that column exists to make a title from memory impossible.
- **Rows (20):**
  - BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210 ("seeing-function"); DEAF|A-NOSOUND|b230 ("hearing-function")
  - VES|A-STABLE|b235 ("vestibular-function"); VES|A-STABLE|d415 ("posture under visual and motion destabilisation")
  - BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330 ("producing speech"), d350 ("conversation")
  - ADHD|A-LOWLOAD|b140 ("attention-function"); DEM|A-LOWLOAD|b144 and BRAIN|A-LOWLOAD|b144 ("memory-function")

  - MH|A-CALM|b152 ("emotional-function"); MH|A-CALM|d240 and AUT|A-CALM|d240 ("stress-handling")
- **Evidence:** `grep -c -i destabilis governance/functional-taxonomy.md` returns 0. A grep of that file for seeing-function, hearing-function, exercise tolerance, energy and drive, and stress-handling also returns nothing.
- **Not checkable from the records:** I did not fetch WHO, so whether each gloss is correct is unverified. `v_lens_crosswalk.icf_title` will show the owner a blank beside these rows, so the warrant gloss is the only title they see.
- **Wider count:** 37 of 135 rows use a NULL-title code (also d230 x7, d310–d329 x2, d330–d349, b117 x4, d166, b435, b440).
- **False if:** `base_icf.title` is populated for these codes with a `title_source`.

### F4. BLOCKER (doctrine, for the owner). 23 rows attach a body-function code to an identity, a class of link the project has not held before
- **Evidence:** `identity_icf_map` holds only d-codes (61 of 61). All b-codes in the batch (rows listed in the closing figures) are new identity-to-impairment links.
- **Basis offered:** for 21 of the 23, the sole basis is the axis register, whose column header is "ICF anchors (findability)". Section 0.5 clause 2 of the same file, marked binding: "Axes describe specifications, not persons … never a portrait."
- **Sharpest cases:**

  - BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|b210, same phrase.
  - MH|A-CALM|b152; ID, DEM and BRAIN with b117.
- **False if:** an owner ruling permits b-codes on identities. I found none in `references/project-standards.md`. I did not sweep `sessions/` for it, so this is not a claim of absence there.

### F5. MUST-AMEND. Every one of the 135 warrants ends with a sentence that review will make false
- **Claim:** "A proposal for the owner's review, not a determination."
- **Failure:** `state` moves to `stated` on owner review and the trigger forbids changing `warrant`. A stated row will permanently say it is not one. It also duplicates `state='pending'` (rule 5).
- **Same class, all 135:**
  - "Judged E2 by session_…" duplicates `created_by_session`.
  - The `E1/E2/E3/M` code is defined only in a comment of an uncommitted scratchpad script. No row or schema object decodes it.
  - A prefix that says what the rest of the cell means is the joined-cell shape the 2026-11-06 schema ruling names.
  - Warrants copy `mapping_confidence`, `mechanism` and `access_need_icf.notes` verbatim. Those cells can change or be retired; the copy cannot.

### F6. MUST-AMEND. 13 of the 32 E1 rows do not meet the script's own definition of E1
- **Definition (script comment):** "the identity's own description names the need".
- **Do meet it:** VES, MOVE, LPA, TALL, BAR (their descriptions name A-STABLE, A-PRECISION, A-SIZE).
- **Do not:**
  - DEAFBLIND|A-TACTILE (3 rows): the description says "centring touch".
  - COM|A-EFFORT (6): the description lists conditions only.
  - EPI|A-TRIGGER (1): "photosensitivity is a relevant subtype".
  - COM|A-TRIGGER (3): "MCAS".
- These are E2 by the definition. The strongest label is on rows that lack its basis.
- **False if:** any of those descriptions contains the need code.

### F7. MUST-AMEND. Four warrants attribute one link's mechanism to two links
- **Rows:** BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|d460 ("link 41/55"); BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|d310–d329 ("42/56"); COM|A-EFFORT|d450 ("43/58"); COM|A-EFFORT|d455 ("44/59").

- **Truth:** links 55 and 56 carry "Sensory — partial vision, contrast, lighting dependency", not "spatial orientation, information access". Links 58 and 59 carry "Fatigue + autonomic — exertion limits", not "Autonomic — activity tolerance, exertion limits, thermal".
- **Command:** `select link_id, mechanism from identity_icf_map where link_id in (41,55,42,56,43,58,44,59)`.

### F8. MUST-AMEND. 78 of 135 rows carry no three-way judgment
- **Shape:** support = "need map". The code-level sentence is "access_need_icf holds N -> code (confirmed)" and is identical for every identity paired with that need. The row is the pair crossed with the need's own rows.

### F9. MUST-AMEND. Codes whose only tie is to the identity, with nothing in the records tying them to the need
The script accepts any code in either map and never asks that it meet the other side.
- DEM|A-PLAIN|d460 and BRAIN|A-PLAIN|d460: "Moving around in different locations" on a plain-language need. d460 is not an AX-COG-L anchor and not in A-PLAIN's map.
- MH|A-CALM|d230 and AUT|A-CALM|d230: d230 anchors AX-STA, THR, CHM and SPR, not AX-ARO. Title NULL.

The view reads the key, not the qualifier.

- CLAUDE.md section 6: "never population umbrellas".

- **SCI|A-REACH.** Links 26 (d465), 23 (d420) and 24 (d450) are the same codes used for MOB|A-REACH. Section 4 maps SCI to "WHM, REA". The description says "paraplegia or tetraplegia".

- **MH|A-STIMULUS|b156.** Section 4 gives MH SPR; AUT, NDV and BRAIN got b156, MH did not.

- **d550.** (A-SELFCARE, d550) is the only non-A-AT need-map row used by no triple. d540 is skipped for MOB and SCI. Every other pair took every need-map code. The exception is unstated.

A-AT's note says "Digital — may be out of built-environment scope; flagged for owner decision", but the batch includes A-TIME ("session timeouts"), A-CALM ("dark patterns") and A-NOSPEECH ("voice-only auth") on the same digital footing.

- AX-COG-L (b117 x4, d166), AX-BAL (b235, d415), AX-COM-E (d330, d350), AX-ARO (b152, d240 x2).

content.content:
## §0.5 The irreducibility principle (governs everything below)

This principle governs how every table, axis, and mapping in this document is to be
read. It is `held-tensions.md` T9 operationalized for the axis model, and it is
binding: no downstream use may read the taxonomy against it.

1. **A spectrum along a spectrum.** Every axis is a continuum, and a person's
   position on it is itself contextual, fluctuating, and fuzzy — not a fixed
   coordinate. The register discretizes for retrieval; the discretization is a
   property of the *tool*, not of the person. `fluctuating: yes/no` is a coarse flag
   over a condition that is, in truth, universal: all function varies by the hour,
   the setting, and the meaning of the task.

2. **Axes describe specifications, not persons.** Per armature §4.2, axes are "the
   dimensions along which built-environment *specifications* vary." They are a
   property of the specification space, not a decomposition of a human being.
   `population_axis_map` (§4) is therefore a **retrieval index and navigation
   hypothesis**, graded by mapping-confidence (§3.2) — **never a portrait**. A person
   is never the join of their axis values, and the taxonomy makes no claim that they
   are.

3. **Measured function is not independent of selfhood.** The same axis value
   manifests differently by fatigue, familiarity, culture, mood, history, and the
   meaning the task holds for the person. This is not a caveat; it is the shared
   claim of three of the project's four declared frameworks — ICF's own
   *capacity vs. performance* gap (what a body can do in a standard room is not what
   this person does in their life), Kawa's inseparable flow of self-context-function,
   and the Capability Approach's conversion factors. No axis value is a stored
   attribute; each is provisional and context-relative.

4. **The person is the ground truth; the specification serves them.** A specification
   is an approximation in service of an individual — a starting hypothesis for a
   conversation, never a verdict about them (mission #7). Person Mode is not the
   exception the model escalates to; it is the reality the model approximates
   (mission #4: the population range "neither bounds nor defines the person"). Every
   default is overridable at the individual value (armature §4.3).

5. **The irreducible remainder has a home.** What no coordinate captures — why two
   people at identical axis values live different lives — is curated in the
   `situations` entity (§5.4) and in Co-1 testimony, which are never subordinated to
   axis-level evidence (§3.1). Their existence in the schema is the project's
   structural admission that the person exceeds the profile.

**Consequence for the enterprise (stated honestly).** Pushed to its end, this
principle is in tension with the whole idea of a specification guide. The project's
answer is that a generalization held *as* a generalization, with the individual as
the override and the ground truth, raises the floor where no individual assessment is
available — which is most of the built world, most of the time. The taxonomy is
legitimate only as an approximation in service of the individual, never as a portrait
of them. Where it is read as a portrait, it is being misused.

**Owner adjudication (2026-07-21).** The enterprise-legitimacy question this principle
raises is settled in favour of proceeding: *something is better than nothing, and a
solution that serves 95% beats one that serves 50%.* The generalization is legitimate
**as the floor**; the individual override (Person Mode, situations, Co-1) carries the
remainder, so shipping the floor is not conceding the tail. This closes the ratified
posture — the taxonomy generalizes openly and declares that it does; it does not wait
for a per-person completeness it can never reach.

## §2 Layer 1 — Functional axes

An **axis** is an architect-actionable person-environment interaction dimension:
an environmental demand that bodies meet variably, which design parameters can
lower, meet, or fail. Axes anchor mechanism and threshold evidence and
`item_taxonomy_links.icf_code` (`item_axis_links` until migration 065 folded it in).
An axis with zero linked slugs or items is a *visible,
queryable coverage hole* — by design.

### §2.1 The axis register (17)

| Axis | Name (interaction-framed) | ICF anchors (findability) | Demand the environment places | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AX-AMB` | Ambulant movement | b770, b730 · d450, d455, d460 | Continuous walking, stairs, distance, gradients — incl. **floor-level living: floor-sitting, prostration, and floor-to-standing transitions** [T1] | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-WHM` | Wheeled movement & transfer | b730, b710 · d465, d420, d410 | Turning, clearance, transfer geometry — independent **and assisted** (two-person, hoist) [T3][T5] | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-REA` | Reach & manipulation | b730, b710 · d440, d445 | Reach envelopes, grip, operating force — at chair, counter, **and floor-level** heights | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-BAL` | Balance & postural demand | b235, b240 · d415, d410 | (a) fall-risk under gait/transfer load; (b) **environments that precipitate dizziness**: repeating pattern, specular floors, glazed edges at height, escalators, large uniform visual fields | STUB |
| `AX-STA` | Sustained-exertion demand | b455, b130 · d230, d450 | Standing, queueing, distance without rest; **grid/lift failure converting routes into exertion cliffs** [T1] | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-PAI` | Pain-load demand | b280 · d410, d450, d640 | Impact, vibration, pressure, cold. Mechanism spans **nociceptive and centrally-sensitized pain** — fibromyalgia-type pain is not nociception-dominant, and provisions must not assume load-avoidance alone suffices | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-THR` | Thermal demand | b550 · d230 | Heat/cold exposure for impaired thermoregulation — via conditioning **and passive means (shading, mass, ventilation) where grids are intermittent** [T1] | PARTIAL |
| `AX-CHM` | Airborne-exposure demand | b435, b440 · d230 | VOCs, fragrance, particulates, smoke | PARTIAL |
| `AX-VIS-L` | Low-vision information demand | b210 · d460, d166 | Environments legible through residual vision: contrast, lighting, glare, size | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-VIS-N` | Non-visual information demand | b210 · d460 | Environments legible without vision: tactile, acoustic, layout consistency | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-AUD` | Auditory access & alerting demand | b230 · d310, d115 | Speech access, alert receipt, assistive listening infrastructure | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-SPR` | Sensory-load demand | b156, b140 · d230, d160 | Stimulus intensity, unpredictability, trigger exposure (incl. photic) — ICF under-represents modulation; anchors are nearest-fit, recorded honestly | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-COG-O` | Orientation demand | b114, b144 · d460, d175 | Legible-space demands: memory, sequencing, decision-point load | ESTABLISHED |
| `AX-COG-L` | Information-access demand | b117, b167 · d166, d310, d315 | Legible-information demands: comprehension load of signage and instructions — **across scripts and literacy levels, not only Easy-Read-genre English** [T1] | STUB |
| `AX-COM-E` | Expressive-communication demand | b320, b330 · d330, d335, d350 | Environments that require producing speech under time/acoustic pressure: counters, intercoms, service interactions; AAC-user dwell and device acoustics. **Signed languages are languages, not deficits: d340 (sign production) is held by the Deaf-community profile (§4), which this axis serves only for sightline/lighting infrastructure** [T2][T3] | STUB |
| `AX-ARO` | Arousal-safety demand | b152 · d240 | Threat-appraisal load: exposure, unpredictability, lack of retreat or exit legibility | STUB |
| `AX-CNT` | Toileting-proximity demand | b620, b525 · d530 | Urgency/frequency as plan-driver: distance, provision count, management space (ostomy/catheter; adult-changing provision as need-driven), **squat and sitting WC typologies both first-class** [T1] | STUB |

**Falsification symmetry [T4].** *Every* axis — established and new alike — carries
a dissolution condition in the staged schema (e.g., AX-AMB/AX-WHM re-merge if
evidence shows no parameter divergence; AX-BAL merges into AX-AMB if precipitant
guidance reduces to fall-prevention parameters). New categories do not audition for
existence under a burden established categories are spared.
## §4 Disposition of the population layer

No rows change until ratification. Canonical sub-code aliases shown where the DB
flattened them. `ALL` is a scope qualifier, not a population
(population-taxonomy §1.3). **Per §0.5, this table is a retrieval index, not a
portrait:** the "maps to" column says which axes a code *indexes into* for evidence
retrieval, graded by mapping-confidence (§3.2) — it does not claim any person
decomposes into those axes, and any individual overrides the mapping.

| Code (DB) | Canonical | Disposition | Maps to | Rationale / fixes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOB | MOB (+MOB/AMB, MOB/UPL) | AXIS-ALIAS | AX-AMB + AX-WHM | Canonical sub-codes already split ambulant/upper-limb; axis layer completes it |
| UPL | MOB/UPL | AXIS-ALIAS | AX-REA | |

| DEAF | DEAF | Dual: axis-alias AX-AUD **+ Deaf-community profile** (identity; no ICD) | AX-AUD | Armature §5 poses this exact open question ("identity-recognition question, not just clinical-framing"); this is the proposed answer. DeafSpace corpus and d340 sign-space provisions are held by the profile — signed language as language, with the axis serving infrastructure only |
| SENS | NDV/SENS | AXIS-ALIAS | AX-SPR | Sub-code was an axis in population clothing; explains its 1-item-link starvation |
| PAIN | PAIN | AXIS-ALIAS | AX-PAI | Mechanism spans nociceptive + central sensitization (§2.1) |

| EPI | (sub-code proposal: NEU/EPI) | PROFILE (diagnostic) | SPR (situational: photic trigger) | Documented judgment call — checklist item |

| CFS | **OFS/ME** | PROFILE (diagnostic) | STA primary | Canonical name is OFS/ME; display "ME/CFS" per community preference. **Post-exertional malaise is a first-class design constraint: environments must not assume exertion is recoverable by rest — distance, queueing, and standing demands are harm vectors, not inconveniences** [T3] |

(v1.0's "de-privileged" phrasing is retracted — the change is structural placement, not standing) [T4] |

content.content:
the taxonomy. A source is only findable if some entity names what it is evidence
*about*; it is only curatable if an entity exists for it to attach *to*.

Axes are framed as **person-environment interaction dimensions** — where a person's
functioning meets an environmental demand — per armature §5 ("Axes are framed as
person-environment interaction dimensions where possible") and the mission's
biopsychosocial ground. The taxonomy names demands the *environment* places on
variable bodies, which is the part designers control; it does not define bodies by
deficit. **[T1][T2]** Where an ICF `b`-code anchor (a body-function code) appears,
it serves *findability* — reaching the clinical literatures indexed that way — and
never serves as a description of any person (population-taxonomy §1.1: codes are
"an organizing convenience, not a definition of people").

## Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (seventh set) — SCI is basically WHEEL and LMB is basically PROSTH: they are the same populations, not additional children (clarifies OI-13)

Given by the owner directly after the sixth set ("SCI and LMB go under MOB"), recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "except SCI is the same as WHEELCHAIR basically and LMB is the same as PROSTHETIC"

**What this records.** The owner's clarification of their own OI-13 answer: `SCI` (people with spinal cord injuries) is, in the owner's word, "basically" the same population as `WHEEL` (wheelchair users), and `LMB` (people with limb differences; upper-limb disabilities, as the registry describes it) is "basically" the same as `PROSTH` (people who use a prosthesis). They do not add two further children to the five in the sixth set; each pair is one population under two names. Rule 5 (one home per fact) therefore applies: a population is held under one code.

**What it does not decide.** (1) Which of each pair's names survives. The owner's decomposition of 2026-11-12 is by device ("wheelchair user, prosthetic device user, other mobility aids"), which is the reading this entry follows. (2) What becomes of the cases the word "basically" leaves out: the registry's `LMB` description includes upper-limb disabilities (a lower-limb prosthesis, which is what `PROSTH` was proposed to cover, is narrower), and a person with an incomplete spinal cord injury may walk (the research memo cites a source that spinal cord injury does not imply a wheelchair); impairment level (paraplegia, quadriplegia) is a descriptor in the medical lens and ICF codes, not an identity code. (3) How the rows now under `SCI` (3 extractions, 9 identity–ICF map rows, 1 population match) and `LMB` (no extractions, 6 identity–ICF map rows) are carried, as the counts stood on 2026-11-12. [ASSUMPTION: the surviving codes are the device codes `WHEEL` and `PROSTH`; `SCI` and `LMB` are retired in favour of them, their rows re-tagged by what each names, and `PROSTH` is described so that it holds what `LMB` held (limb differences, upper and lower, and prosthetic devices) unless the owner narrows it; unratified.]

OI-13: SCI is the same population as WHEEL and LMB is the same population as PROSTH; each pair is held under one code
OI-13 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

CONDITION: any session writing the mobility family's registry rows, retiring `SCI` or `LMB`, or tagging a figure that names a spinal cord injury, a limb difference, a prosthesis or a wheelchair.
ACTION: (1) Hold each pair under one code, the device code, and retire the other by the sanctioned verb with its successor. (2) Describe `PROSTH` so it holds what `LMB` held, or report the case it leaves out. (3) Re-tag the rows under `SCI` and `LMB` by what each names; do not fan out a grade. (4) Keep impairment level in the medical lens and ICF codes. (5) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified. This supersedes, on the point of `SCI` and `LMB` being additional children, the sixth set's account of the family.

## Owner clarification 2026-11-12 (eighth set) — LMB becomes UPL (upper limb) and is not part of mobility; only SCI is the same as WHEEL

Given by the owner directly after the seventh set, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim, in the order sent:

> "LMB should be UPL for upper limb then"

> "and that doesnt concern mobility"

**What this records.** The owner corrects the seventh set's pairing of `LMB` with `PROSTH`. `LMB` (registry: "people with limb differences; upper-limb disabilities") is to be **`UPL`, for upper limb**, and it **does not concern mobility**: it is not a child of `MOB` and it is not the same population as `PROSTH`. What stands from the seventh set is that `SCI` is basically the same population as `WHEEL`. The mobility family is therefore the parent `MOB` with the device children `WHEEL` (which takes in `SCI`), `PROSTH` and `WALKAID`. The sixth set's placing of `LMB` under `MOB` is set aside by this entry.

**What it does not decide.** (1) How `LMB` becomes `UPL`: a rename of the code, or a new code with `LMB` retired to it (the registry's code is a key that identity–ICF map rows point at; there are 6 such rows and no extractions on `LMB` as of 2026-11-12). (2) The display name and description of `UPL` (the registry's present description combines limb differences and upper-limb disabilities). (3) The cases at the edge: a lower-limb difference in a person who uses no prosthesis (not upper limb, and no aid), an upper-limb prosthesis user (upper limb, not mobility), and whether an upper-limb disability that affects reach is a lens on reach and manipulation parameters (it is the owner's existing `upper-limb-impairment-built-environment` topic). [ASSUMPTION: `UPL` is a population in the identity lens like the others and keeps `LMB`'s ICF map rows; the lower-limb difference without a prosthesis is placed by the T-102 design on `MOB` with ICF d4 codes, and an upper-limb prosthesis user on `UPL`; unratified.]

OI-13: SCI is the same population as WHEEL; LMB becomes UPL (upper limb) and is not part of the mobility family; PROSTH is a device child of MOB, separate from UPL
OI-13 STATUS: ANSWERED BY THE OWNER

CONDITION: any session writing the mobility family's rows, retiring `SCI`, or renaming, retiring or tagging `LMB` or `UPL`.
ACTION: (1) Hold `SCI` and `WHEEL` as one population under `WHEEL`. (2) Make `LMB` into `UPL` (upper limb), outside the mobility family, by the sanctioned verb with the successor if it is a new code; move its map rows without duplicating. (3) Do not describe `PROSTH` as holding what `LMB` held. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified. This supersedes the seventh set's pairing of `LMB` with `PROSTH` and the sixth set's placing of `LMB` under `MOB`.

**What this settles.** The lower-limb child of `MOB` is **`LLD`, people with lower-limb differences**, replacing the proposed `PROSTH`. It is defined by the condition (a lower-limb difference), not by the device, so it holds people who use a lower-limb prosthesis and people with a lower-limb difference who use none. It is the lower-limb counterpart of `UPL` (upper limb, outside mobility). The mobility family is therefore the parent `MOB` with the children `WHEEL` (which takes in `SCI`), `LLD` and `WALKAID`. This departs, for this one child, from the owner's earlier decomposition "by device" (wheelchair user, prosthetic device user, other mobility aids); the owner chose it knowing so.

**What it does not decide.** (1) That a lower-limb prosthesis is a device and is held in `device_class` (the T-102 design proposed adding `lower_limb_prosthesis`, `crutches` and `cane`): with `LLD` defined by the condition, whether the prosthesis value remains in `device_class` as a descriptor of a figure or participants is for the design to restate, keeping one home per fact. (2) The registry description of `LLD`. (3) Whether the old `LMB` rows' lower-limb content goes to `LLD` and its upper-limb content to `UPL`: `LMB` was described as "people with limb differences; upper-limb disabilities", and the owner has made `LMB` into `UPL`; the 6 identity–ICF map rows on `LMB` (as of 2026-11-12) have to be placed on `UPL` or `LLD` by what each names. [ASSUMPTION: the identity codes are not mutually exclusive, so a person with a lower-limb difference who also uses a wheelchair or walking aid is in `LLD` and in `WHEEL` or `WALKAID`; unratified.]

## Owner statement 2026-11-12 (thirteenth) — MOB decomposes into more specific identity populations

Made in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`), while the decision about carrying the rows written under `MOB` (OD-14) was being prepared for the owner, recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Quoted verbatim:

> "MOB is more difficult than other categories in that it decomposes into more specific identity populations (e.g. prosthetics vs wheelchairs vs other mobility aids, power wheelchair vs manual wheelchair, paraplegia vs quadraplegia)"

**What this records.** The mobility identity is a family and not one population: it divides by the aid a person uses (a prosthesis, a wheelchair, other mobility aids), within wheelchairs by drive (power or manual), and by the level of impairment (paraplegia or quadriplegia, spelled by the owner "quadraplegia"). It is harder than the other identity categories because of this depth. The owner's examples are examples ("e.g."), not a closed list.

**What it does not decide.** Which of these divisions become identity codes, which stay descriptions of a study's participants or of a device (the extraction's `device_class` already holds one of them), how deep the hierarchy goes, whether the 2026-08-25 two-way split into ambulant people and wheelchair users stands as the first division or is superseded by a deeper one, and what a row written under `MOB` is carried as. These bear on OD-14 and on the population taxonomy, which is the owner's. [ASSUMPTION: the statement is a description of the domain that widens the question OD-14 asks, not an answer to it, and it does not by itself supersede the 2026-08-25 ruling.]

CONDITION: any session splitting, tagging or carrying the mobility identity, or reading a figure's population under `MOB`.
ACTION: (1) Treat `MOB` as a family with more than two levels of division, not as a pair. (2) Do not assume the two-way split is the whole decomposition. (3) Keep a division that describes a device or a participant's level in one home only (rule 5), and decide with the owner whether it is an identity code or a descriptor. (4) Treat the [ASSUMPTION] mark above as unratified.

> "use advocacy groups and disability ethics as a lens for grouping/sorting/taxonomy"

**What this records.** How disabled people organise themselves through their own advocacy groups, and what disability ethics proposes, are to be the lens through which the project groups, sorts and classifies people. It is stated as a method for the analysis of the taxonomy and says nothing yet about which categories result.

**What it does not decide.** Which advocacy groups count, how their categories are turned into codes, how the ethical approaches are weighed where they disagree, and which of the registry's present identity codes change. The population taxonomy remains the owner's. It does not supersede the 2026-08-28 ruling that a determination is keyed on four lens columns, nor the project's rule to work from the ICF and access-need frame; it is a lens on how the groupings within them are drawn. Given by the owner in reply to prompts on the population-umbrellas memo (`workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/POPULATION-UMBRELLAS-MEMO.md`), put to them in the session that audited the pipeline (`session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit`). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/retired_vocabulary_audit.py — flag text that is READABLE AND WRONG.

WHY THIS EXISTS
---------------
The expensive failure in this repo is not that old files exist. It is that a
session greps for a fact, gets several answers, and cannot tell which is
current. Three worked examples, all real:

  * `audit.yml` was folded into `ci.yml` on 2026-08-01. Dozens of live documents
    still name it. CLAUDE.md §0 named it too, and in doing so contradicted its
    own §7 two hundred lines below, for a day.
  * `applicable_groups` is a column that no longer exists. `migrate_items.py`
    took no required arguments, opened the canonical database immediately, and
    was saved from writing it ONLY because it crashed on that column name.
  * A skill instructed sessions to open `/tmp/guidebook.db`. That path does not
    exist, so the failure reads as a broken environment rather than a wrong
    instruction.

Each is a rule that lives only as prose, and prose does not check itself. This
promotes the rule to level 2 on the enforcement spectrum (CLAUDE.md §2: text
rule -> audit script), and registration in governance/check-registry.yaml takes
it to level 3.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
-------------------
It does not sweep history. `_archived/`, `sessions/`, `decisions/`,
`scripts/migrations/` and the dated audit reports are exempt by default,
because rewriting them would contradict the forward-only, immutable-record
convention that DR-2026-07-21 §4 invoked when it refused to rewrite `E-##` in
past records, and that CLAUDE.md §4 states for migrations.

It also does not decide what is retired. That lives in
governance/retired-vocabulary.yaml, which carries the admission test, the
authority for each entry, and — importantly — the `deferred:` and `rejected:`
sections recording what was considered and NOT added. Read those before
extending the register; three of the obvious candidates are traps.

Adversarial pass 2: `/home/user/guidebook/scripts/migrations/data_20261121013428_2026-11-21-identity-need-icf-triples.sql` (read-only)

Method: I applied the SQL to a scratch copy of the DB (foreign keys on; it applies cleanly) and checked the rows it produced against the live DB, `governance/functional-taxonomy.md`, `references/website/data/populations.json`, the ledger and the earlier pass's transcript. Nothing in the repo was written. Row ids are identity|need|code.

The migration holds 82 triples (49 e-code, 33 d-code, 0 b-code), 4 gaps, 1 pass and 14 findings. Re-derive rather than trust: `select substr(icf_code,1,1), count(*) from identity_need_icf group by 1`.

---

## Blockers: rulings already made that the migration writes against

### B1. Warrants rest on the axes layer, which the owner retired
- **Rows carrying a literal `AX-` string (14):** BLIND|A-NOSIGHT|d460, VES|A-STABLE|d415, BRAIN|A-STABLE|d415, BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330, BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d350, MOVE|A-PRECISION|d440, AUT|A-STIMULUS|d230, MH|A-STIMULUS|d230, MH|A-CALM|d240, AUT|A-CALM|d240, and four that copy "beyond AX-CNT" from `access_need_icf.notes` (MOB, SCI and LMB|A-SELFCARE|d510, LMB|A-SELFCARE|d540).
- **Rows whose only basis is an axis anchor (7):** VES|A-STABLE|d415, BRAIN|A-STABLE|d415, BRAIN|A-NOSPEECH|d330 and d350, MOVE|A-PRECISION|d440, MH|A-CALM|d240, AUT|A-CALM|d240.
- **Rows citing "functional-taxonomy.md 4 maps X to Y" with bare axis codes (15):** the codes are BAL, WHM, REA, CHM, ARO, COM-E and VIS-N x AUD. Eight of them also name retired population codes (DBL, NEU, PCS-TBI).
- **Rulings:**
  - `references/project-standards.md:800-811`, owner 2026-08-24: "I don't want axis to be used".
  - `references/project-standards.md:3398-3399`, owner 2026-09-13: "'AX-' for ICF should never ever exist anywhere."
  - `scripts/migrations/109_drop_axes.sql` dropped `axes`, `population_axis_map` and `access_need_axis_map`.
  - `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/RULINGS.md:248` (R35): sentences in functional-taxonomy "that treat axes as live are stale".
- **What a reader takes:** "AX-VIS-N (status ESTABLISHED)" reads as a live, ratified object. This is the F13 repair, and it presents a dropped layer's status as current.
- **No gate sees it:** `scripts/audit/retired_vocabulary_audit.py` exempts `scripts/migrations/` and `.db` files (lines 29 and 77 of that script).
- **Same basis under the gap:** 22 of the 24 withheld rows are "taxonomy anchor" rows, so GAP-377 asks the owner about rows built on the retired layer.
- **Command:** `grep -o "AX-[A-Z-]*" <migration> | sort | uniq -c`; `select ... from identity_need_icf where warrant like '%AX-%'` returns 14.
- **False if:** a later owner ruling restored axes as a citable basis. `git grep` over the ledger headings and for "axis" found none.

### B2. MOVE and VES are keyed as identities; the owner ruled they are access needs
- **Rows (4):** MOVE|A-PRECISION|d440, MOVE|A-PRECISION|e115, VES|A-STABLE|d415, VES|A-STABLE|e240.
- **Rulings:**
  - `references/project-standards.md:6015` onward (third set, OD-37), owner quoted: "MOVE and VES are access needs, agreed." ACTION (2): "Move `MOVE` and `VES` to the access-need frame."
  - `references/project-standards.md:8012`, OD-67, ratified 2026-11-19: "yes, one answer on the full list, VES withheld". That list is the batch re-deriving ICF rows for ADHD, DeafBlind, epilepsy, MS and vestibular "from the retired axis map".
- **Why it passed:** `base_taxonomy_identity` still shows both `active` with `superseded_by_need` NULL, so the registry lags the ruling and the generator's "active identity" test passes on it.
- **Also:** VES|A-STABLE|d415 is exactly the re-derivation OD-67 withheld, and d415's title is NULL (the OD-67 batch is the task that titles it).
- **False if:** a ruling after 2026-11-12 restored MOVE or VES as identities. `grep -n -E '\bVES\b|\bMOVE\b'` past line 6040 finds only the OD-67 line.

### B3. Nine SCI rows were added by the F11 repair against the mobility-family rulings; three carry a false tie
- **Rows (9):** SCI|A-REACH|d465, d420, d450, e120, e155; SCI|A-SELFCARE|d510, d530, e115, e340.
- **Rulings:**
  - `references/project-standards.md:6111` (seventh set): SCI is "basically" the same population as wheelchair users, "each pair is one population under two names", "a population is held under one code", "do not fan out a grade".
  - Eighth set ACTION (1): "Hold `SCI` and `WHEEL` as one population under `WHEEL`."
